method: Whitespace is removed from a sequence of 1-64 binary digits. NRZ-L maps 0 to low (-1) and 1 to high (+1). NRZ-I starts low, changes level at the start of a 1 and holds the previous level for a 0. Manchester follows IEEE 802.3: 0 is low-to-high and 1 is high-to-low. Differential Manchester starts low, always changes at mid-bit, adds a start-bit transition for 0 and no start-bit transition for 1. Bipolar AMI holds zero for 0 and maps successive 1 bits to alternating full-bit positive and negative pulses, starting positive. Each bit is represented by two half-bit levels; transitions count changes between adjacent levels, and the mean is their arithmetic average. The SVG waveform and copyable level list are deterministic and use only normalized -1, 0 and +1 values. No data is stored or transmitted.

sources.title: IEEE 802.3 Manchester convention: 0 is low-to-high and 1 is high-to-low
Differential Manchester: mid-bit clock transition; 0 has a start-bit transition and 1 does not
Bipolar AMI: zero bits use zero level and successive marks alternate polarity
